## Work log

<!-- Chronological, written as you go. What was actually done, why, what it cost.

- **Polished the *Visa for a Hilsa* v2 script** against the comic playbook, as was done for *Snow*
  ([plan](../plans/2026-10-02_sam-feedback-snow-hilsa.plan.md)). It has 7 boards, 36 panels and
  20–116 words a page.
  - Added an ASCII grid for each page, pinned looks for the cast and Shapla's three foremothers,
    the through-lines (the brass pot, the tag, two fixed camera positions on the hut) and the
    lettering rules.
  - Two new cast members to make before building: *the brass pot* and *Jalal and Shapla's hut*.
  - Fixed playbook breaks in the draft. The page 2 telemetry had been drawn into the art; it is
    now lettered labels. "Out of frame" and "glow" were in prompts.
  - Ya's tablet is now her e-paper notebook from *Snow*, and Taro appears on every page from 2 on.
  - Page 5's punchline is one large silent panel. On page 7, Ya leaving and Jalal's outburst
    share one panel, so the final boat gets half the board.
  - Edited Drafts now has a "Scene 0: Story of the Wife (TBW)" heading, which the prologue fills.
  - At Yan's request, wrote it into the *Script: Visa for a Hilsa* tab above Version 1, using
    `script-to-doc.py`. Nothing in the tab was changed.
- **Built *Visa for a Hilsa* on A1** (`VH`, `d89a6f17…`): 7 boards, 36 panels, each page
  lettered and checked in Chrome.
  - New cast: *the brass pot* and *Jalal and Shapla's hut*. Jalal (moustache, white vest) and
    Shapla (green sari, low bun) got pinned descriptions and new sheets. All four sheets were
    clean first time.
  - Redraws:
    - 1.8: two fish instead of one.
    - 2.2: a blank teal band and garbled drawn words. 2.3 and 2.5: brown hilsa instead of silver.
    - 3.4 and 3.6: no room for lettering. 3.6 again: Ya's hologram came out in full colour, fixed
      by leaving her out of `cast`.
    - 4.4: blank. 4.5: drawn notebook label, sub-panels, faces at the top, then green walls.
    - 5.1: strangers instead of Jalal and Shapla. 5.3: green walls. 5.4: Ya drawn as a man, and a
      drawn strip.
    - 6.3: green walls. 7.4: the boat's direction (three tries).
  - Open for Yan: in 7.4 the boat still heads left, towards the village Shapla looks back at.
  - Five new rows in the playbook's table of fixes; canon production state updated.
- **Redrew the Sunda maps (PAO:3:1, 3:2) from real geodata**
  ([plan](../plans/2026-10-03_sunda-geodata-maps.plan.md)). `scripts/sunda-maps.py` takes ETOPO
  2022, contours the −120 m lowstand coast, and routes flow over the exposed shelf. The drowned
  rivers come out of the data rather than being traced from the copyrighted moodboard maps.
  - It reproduced the reconstructions: a Gulf of Thailand paleo-lake, the Siam river joining the
    North Sunda trunk, and a mouth about 60 km from the flotel's 5°N 110°E.
  - Both maps are in the panels via `draw_panel_svg`, with labels as size-11 caption balloons.
  - Still open: "Pangaea's largest" in caption 3:2 is wrong by about 200 million years, and that
    caption runs under the top of its panel.
  - Started a Homebrew reinstall of GDAL (the old 3.3.2 had lost its poppler library), at Yan's
    request. ~~Homebrew~~ It failed: Homebrew no longer ships Intel-Mac bottles, and the source
    build died. Resolved with conda-forge instead: GDAL 3.13.3 (plus the netCDF, HDF5 and PDF
    drivers) in a micromamba env at `~/micromamba/envs/gdal`. The tools are symlinked into
    `~/.local/bin`, which comes before the still-broken brew 3.3.2 on PATH.
- **Pennant captions** ([plan](../plans/2026-10-03_pointed-captions.plan.md)). A caption can now
  have a pointed end (`point: left | right`) and a tilt (`rotation`, until now sfx-only), set from
  the inspector or the MCP. Lettering stays out of the art, so Sam's text stays editable.
  Deployed to production. The two PAO:4:2 captions are now tilted pennants, as in Sam's
  inspiration image.
  - The e2e test is written but has not run (it needs local Supabase, and Docker was down).
- **PAO:3:4** redrawn: everyday clothes (some everyday traditional wear, no costumes), a crowd
  that reflects the world's population, and Isma (18) and Dew (63) at the centre.
  **PAO:4:5**: the PESA agent is now Black. **PAO:3:2**: a bolder Sunda Summit marker.
- **PAO page 6: a second version of page 5**, recreating Sam's "The Pluriverse in Microcosm"
  infographic (slide `h131ac5edd0a73ed9_0_53`). The art is a glass-sphere watershed on the
  waterline, chained to the seabed. Sam's slide text is lettered on top: principles as cream
  circles, institutions as teal circles, systems as ochre boxes, and the purpose on a pennant.
  Page 5 is unchanged, so Yan can pick one.
  - Slide text slip: PROSPER's box repeats PESA's subtitle and description, so page 6 uses page 5's
    PROSPER text. PESA is "denizen-support" on the slide but "customer-support" on page 5.
- **PAO:2:6** redrawn so Isma and Dew are small in the crowd: at that size they were being read as
  the banker and the Summit speaker.
- **PAO:6:1** redrawn with the composition moved up: smaller sphere, short chain, and the anchor rock on
  the seabed visible between the bottom boxes.
